full_judgment: 10. The learned Advocate for the petitioners referred to the following decisions in support of his contention. These decisions are 28 DLR 252. 27 DLR. 232, 27 DLR 683 and I DLR 26. In the Case of Azizur Rahman Vs. Janata Bank reported in 28 DLR 252, it was held that:—"The scope of section 151 is often misunderstood by the courts below Section 151 clearly provides for such an application only when the courts find that prevention of abuse of the process of the court is necessary or where for the ends of justice an order on an application is necessary to be made. In the garb of an order being necessary for the ends of justice cannot negative the remedies available under the Code itself. The appeals or for that matter revisions under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure are provided for to meet situations in which some injustice is felt to have been made to party in a proceeding. This phraseology for the end of justice is not an omnibus remedy given to the courts where a final order has been passed to rectify a wrong as may be necessary for the ends of justice. An application under section 151 of the Code should be used in a limited and in a sparing manner and must be avoided in a case where the Code provides for appeal or for revision." In the case of Rajendra Shirai; and others Vs Mahadev Shirali reported in 27 DLR 232, it was held :—"The powers. as contemplated in the section, 151 C.P. Code are intended to supplement the other provisions of the Code as a Legislature cannot forsee and provide for every eventuality which may occur, but they are not for the purpose of evading or ignoring the express pro-visions of the law or for inventing a new procedure according to the individual inclination of a particular judge. Under the cover of these powers a court cannot override the express provisions of the law applicable to a particular case. These powers cannot be invoked in a case which is fully covered by a specific provision in the Code, or, where there is a positive prohibition regarding a particular act or order or where there in alternative remedy". . In the case of Mst. Masuda Khartum & ors. Vs. Maniruzzaman reported in 27 DLR 683, it was held that : "The application for restoration is under Order 9, rule 4 and under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is undauntedly misconceived. Order 9, rule 4 of Civil Procedure Code provides for the plaintiff to bring a fresh suit which is dismissed either for non-service of summons in consequence of plaintiff's failure to pay cost or for non-appearance of both the plaintiffs and defendant. An application under section 151 C.P,C. is not maintainable. Prayer under section 151 was deleted on the application filed by the defendant himself. It is thus not clear under what provisions of law the court has granted the prayer of the defendant restoring the application. It may be presumed that the court purported to act under section 151 C.P C. It appears clear that there were good grounds for restoration of the case under Order 9, rule 13 and therefore there is no need to exercise the power vested in the Supreme Court under section 115 C.P.C." In the case of Musst Mansura Khatun & ors. Vs. Muhammad Raja Meah and ors. reports. in I DLR 26, it was held that: "When a party has got a right of appeal against an order he cannot main-tain an application under section 151 C.P.C. for reversal of that order and that the trial court acted in the exercise of its jurisdiction with material irregularity in entertaining the said application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure". From the decisions quoted above it is clear that when a party had got a right of appeal against the Order he should go for an appeal, he cannot maintain as application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for reversal of the exparte order. In the instant case, the learned Munsif did exercise his jurisdiction with material irregularity in allowing the said application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It was just and proper for restoration of a case under Order 9, r. 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure but it is not just and proper to entertain the application for restoration under Order 9, rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure and under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Order 7, rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for the plaintiff to bring a fresh suit which is dismissed either for non-service of summons in consequence of plaintiff's failure to pay cost or for non-appearance of both the plaintiff and defendants. In this connection, an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is also not maintainable, because inherent power of the court exists only where there is no express provision of law applicable to the case. The provisions of this section cannot be invoked to defeat the provisions of the Code nor can be invoked to further injustice or to condone gross negligence. The court cannot interfere under section 151 of the Code with appealable order.
